defects.problem: The initial solo statement and the returning main-theme statement are mapped with cellos and basses active from the start. The cited score instead rests both low-string staves through the opening solo bars; they enter later in the phrase. This is the same distinction already respected in the Rondo’s opening snapshot.
defects.evidence: https://imslp.org/wiki/Clarinet_Concerto_in_A_major,_K.622_(Mozart,_Wolfgang_Amadeus) — Breitkopf 1881 score, PDF p. 5 (printed 211), first Solo, and PDF p. 21 (printed 227), returning theme: violin I, violin II and viola accompany while cello and contrabass rest initially.
defects.fix: Remove cellos and basses from the initial states at 100 and 510 seconds and qualify the notes to say that low strings join later. Alternatively add a later, separately justified state for their return; do not imply that they sound throughout the solo theme’s opening.

defects.problem: The 280-second role-reversal passage is scored for solo clarinet and strings, not flutes, bassoons and horns. All three wind/brass families rest across the cited later solo-exposition pages. The following orchestral ritornello already has its own fuller state at 320 seconds.
